notes: The page opens with the asserted relation σ_infinity(g^{-1}) = l_0^β g l_1^β and says that it determines β uniquely as a function of g. This is a transcription of the author’s assertion, not an independent proof.

The abandoned central argument invokes a relation called fondamentale and derives an image of L_1 under u, followed by a modulo qualification involving right multiplication by an element of L_1. Its rightmost image index is blackened, and an expression after déjà is separately cancelled inside the cancelled block.

The first product of the abandoned relation is g-shaped in the ink, although uρ is the mathematically expected form suggested by the surrounding discussion. That expectation was used only to articulate the alternative, not to replace the ink. Root independently reviewed the crop and concurred on u\unsure{g|\rho}. The surviving le donnée is an apparent authorial grammatical slip and is left unchanged. No terminal stop after u is supplied.

The lower paragraph proposes more attractive generators of a sous-extension of the ornamental S_3 by π, adding dans Aut_lac(π) interlinearly. The article before extension contains both an a-shaped baseline body and an apostrophe-like upper trace; no correction sequence can be established, so la/l' remains uncertain.

The author invokes ramification groups at 0, 1, infinity and describes them as canonically isomorphic to the hatted integer group. The manuscript ends that clause with a comma. It then defines ε_0, ε_1, ε_infinity by the three square relations and begins a more precise characterization through an automorphism class modulo π, fixing l_i, with a doubtful lower insertion reading de carré l_i.

No explicit authorial doubt phrase, date, or diagram occurs on this leaf. Handwritten manuscript page number 11 is in the lower-left margin and is omitted in H. The editorial scan identifier 12 is not an inscription. The first page reader performed no mathematical verification; separate main-reader checks are recorded below.

Main-reader inspection of the cancelled fundamental relation finds a right-sided head and hooked descending tail after u, closer to the local g than to the following rho, whose stem descends on the left. The diplomatic reading therefore puts g first while retaining rho as an alternative. The earlier uρ=int(g)ρu supplies the mathematical expectation; it does not authorize replacing the visible g-like form. The nonstandard le donnée is plainly written and is preserved.

Main-reader local algebra check of the two adjacent product formulas: σ₀σ₁=l₁⁻¹ρ gives ρ=l₁σ₀σ₁ by multiplication on the left. The following written ρ=σ₀σ₁l₁ would require l₁ to commute with σ₀σ₁. Thus the stated i.e. is not a valid noncommutative rearrangement without an additional commutation condition. Both written product orders are retained, and this note records only the necessary algebraic qualification.

The blind audit restores a separate g between the nested int(g) cancellation and modulo; the broad paragraph cancellation is certain, but the additional local strike may or may not include this g. It also places the t of élt on the baseline and removes the unwritten final stop after the live p.ex abbreviation. The opening cancelled verb, the overwritten par/près/puis, the unindexed pi/Pi forms, the à/colon sign, and the local cancellation state of the final sigma/de-shaped form remain qualified. The local noncommutative product check above is unchanged; these new decisions are paleographic, not additional mathematical verifications.

The lower crossed strokes remain compatible with élt, but do not expose every letter securely enough to remove the doubt.

differences.final: dans la classe mod $\unsure{\pi|\Pi}$ des $\sigma_i$, \deleted{et} qui fixe $l_i$ et est \unsure{\deleted{\unsure{de|$\sigma$}}|$\sigma$} \inserted{\unsure{de carré $l_i$}}
differences.adjudication: Retain la classe mod, qualify pi case, and reopen the final sign’s cancellation state.
differences.ink: After dans the low article body is a, followed by c, a tall l, and connected a/s/s/e, then m/o/d. The group sign has a capped upright body with a hooked inner/right leg and does not securely distinguish pi from capital Pi. The et after sigma-i is definitely crossed. At the far right, by contrast, the long upper stroke can be the cap of a live sigma-shaped form rather than an independent strike through de; both readings remain possible. The lower de carré and looped l survive, but the index is compressed at the clipped edge. Root also consulted the already saved first-pass close crop of this same ending.
